title: Alcohol, Stimulants, Sedatives and Opioids: Naloxone at PCP Level
next: Chapter 36, Lesson 3: Gases, pesticides, household poisons, prescription drugs and bites

slides.title: Today's lesson
slides.body:
As an EMR you already ventilate with a BVM and give naloxone IM or IN. Today, as a PCP:

  1. Recognize and support alcohol and sedative overdose and withdrawal
  2. Manage the agitated stimulant or hallucinogen patient with the BC exam tools
  3. Run the BC Suspected Narcotic Overdose protocol, with IV naloxone

Textbook: Chapter 36, PDF pages 3127–3188 (Alcohol to Opioids)
slides.say: Welcome back. Today we cover the substances people use and misuse: alcohol, stimulants, cannabis, hallucinogens, sedatives and opioids. As EMRs, you already ventilate with a bag-valve mask and give naloxone by injection or nasal spray, and that stays the core of opioid care. As a PCP, three things change. You'll recognize the dangerous phases of alcohol and sedative use, including withdrawal. You'll manage agitated stimulant patients knowing which textbook drugs aren't on the BC licensing exam. And you'll run the BC narcotic overdose protocol with a new option: IV naloxone for the patient who stays unconscious and isn't breathing.
slides.sayZh: 欢迎回来。今天讲人们使用和滥用的物质：酒精、兴奋剂、大麻、致幻剂、镇静药和阿片类。作为 EMR，你们已经会用球囊面罩通气，会肌注或鼻喷纳洛酮，这仍然是阿片类处理的核心。作为 PCP，有三点变化：你要认出酒精和镇静药使用中的危险阶段，包括戒断；你要处理激越的兴奋剂病人，同时清楚教材里哪些药执照考试不考；你还要按 BC 阿片过量流程处理，多了一个新选项：对始终昏迷、没有呼吸的病人静脉给纳洛酮。

slides.title: Alcohol: intoxication and hidden dangers
slides.body:
• Most abused drug in Canada; acts like any CNS depressant
  • Biggest threats: slow breathing and aspiration of vomit
  • Chronic use: GI bleeding, low sugar, falls with subdural bleeds
  • Also pneumonia, burns, hypothermia, arrhythmias
  • Care: left side, suction, O₂, assist ventilation, check BGL

The smell of alcohol is not a diagnosis. Look for what lies underneath.
slides.say: Alcohol is the most abused drug in Canada, and severe intoxication is a poisoning like any other central nervous system depressant. The biggest dangers are slow breathing and aspiration, because the gag reflex is suppressed. Long-term heavy drinking adds more risks: GI bleeding, low blood sugar from liver damage, and falls with bleeding under the skull, called a subdural hematoma, plus pneumonia, burns and hypothermia. Your care is EMR care done carefully: if the gag reflex is intact, place the patient on the left side with suction ready, give oxygen, assist ventilation if needed, and check the glucose. As a PCP, keep asking what else could explain the picture.
slides.sayZh: 酒精是加拿大滥用最多的药物，严重醉酒和其他中枢神经抑制剂一样是一种中毒。最大的危险是呼吸变慢和误吸，因为呕吐反射被抑制了。长期大量饮酒带来更多风险：消化道出血、肝损伤导致的低血糖、跌倒后颅骨下出血（硬膜下血肿），还有肺炎、烧伤和低体温。你的处理就是认真做好 EMR 的基本功：呕吐反射还在就让病人左侧卧、备好吸引，给氧，必要时辅助通气，并测血糖。作为 PCP，要一直追问：还有什么能解释这个表现？

slides.title: Alcohol withdrawal: seizures and DTs
slides.body:
Withdrawal seizuresabout 12–48 h after the last drinkusually brief, self-limiting
Delirium tremens (DTs)48–72 h; sometimes 7–10 daysmortality up to 15%
  • DTs: confusion, tremor, fever, sweating, fast pulse, terrifying hallucinations
  • BP high early, then low from dehydration
  • Protect from injury; calm, reorient, O₂
  • PCP: IV; book gives normal saline for dehydration
slides.say: Stopping alcohol suddenly after long heavy use can be more dangerous than drinking. Withdrawal seizures usually come about twelve to forty-eight hours after the last drink, and most are brief and stop on their own. Delirium tremens, or DTs, usually starts forty-eight to seventy-two hours after the last drink, sometimes as late as seven to ten days, and the death rate can reach fifteen percent. Picture confusion, tremor, fever, sweating, a fast pulse and terrifying hallucinations. The blood pressure is often high at first, then falls as the patient dehydrates. Protect them from injury, speak calmly, reorient them often, and give oxygen. As a PCP, start an IV; the book gives normal saline for dehydration.
slides.sayZh: 长期大量饮酒后突然停酒，可能比喝酒更危险。戒断抽搐通常出现在最后一次饮酒后约十二到四十八小时，多数短暂、会自行停止。震颤谵妄（DTs）通常在最后一次饮酒后四十八到七十二小时开始，有时迟至七到十天，死亡率可达百分之十五。表现为意识混乱、震颤、发热、大汗、心率快和恐怖的幻觉。血压起初常偏高，随着脱水又下降。要防止病人受伤，语气平静，反复帮他定向，并给氧。作为 PCP，开静脉；书里对脱水给生理盐水。

slides.title: Stimulants: cocaine, meth, bath salts
slides.body:
• Fast pulse, big pupils, sweaty, agitated, BP usually high
  • Killers: arrhythmia, MI, stroke, seizure, hyperthermia
  • Meth lasts up to 12 h; bath salts → excited delirium
  • Care: safety, airway, O₂ to SpO₂ ≥ 94%, active cooling
  • PCP: IV; normal saline for hypotension
  • Book's first-line benzodiazepine: not on the BC exam
slides.say: Stimulants like cocaine, methamphetamine and bath salts flood the body with adrenaline-like chemicals. Expect a fast pulse, big pupils, sweating, agitation, and usually high blood pressure. The killers are heart rhythm problems, heart attack, stroke, seizures and a dangerously high temperature. Smoked crack acts within seconds; methamphetamine lasts up to twelve hours; and bath salts can cause excited delirium, with surprising strength. Scene safety comes first, with police support if needed. Then manage the airway, give oxygen to ninety-four percent or more, and cool a hot patient with ice packs and misting. As a PCP, start an IV and give normal saline for low blood pressure. The book's first-line drug is a benzodiazepine, which isn't on the BC licensing exam.
slides.sayZh: 可卡因、甲基苯丙胺和「浴盐」这类兴奋剂让体内充满类似肾上腺素的物质。会看到心率快、瞳孔大、出汗、激越，血压通常偏高。致命的是心律失常、心梗、卒中、抽搐和危险的高体温。吸食快克几秒内起效；甲基苯丙胺可持续十二小时；浴盐可引起兴奋性谵妄，力气大得惊人。现场安全第一，需要时叫警察支援。然后管理气道，给氧使血氧达到九十四以上，用冰袋和喷雾给高热病人降温。作为 PCP，开静脉，低血压时给生理盐水。书里的一线药是苯二氮卓类，执照考试不考。

slides.q: A man who has used methamphetamine for three days is agitated, sweating and hot to touch. HR 148, BP 172/100. On the BC licensing exam, which of these textbook treatments is NOT available to a PCP?
options: Oxygen to keep SpO₂ at 94% or higher
Active cooling with ice packs and misting
An IV with normal saline if his BP falls
A benzodiazepine to calm him and prevent seizures
slides.say: Let's check the exam rules. A man who has used methamphetamine for three days is agitated, sweating and hot to touch. His heart rate is one hundred forty-eight and his blood pressure is one seventy-two over one hundred. On the BC licensing exam, which of these textbook treatments is not available to a PCP? A, oxygen to keep the saturation at ninety-four percent or higher. B, active cooling with ice packs and misting. C, an IV with normal saline if his blood pressure falls. D, a benzodiazepine to calm him and prevent seizures. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 检查一下考试规则。一名男子连续三天使用甲基苯丙胺，激越、大汗、摸上去很烫，心率一百四十八，血压一百七十二比一百。按 BC 执照考试，下列教材里的处理哪一项 PCP 不能用？A 给氧使血氧保持九十四以上；B 用冰袋和喷雾主动降温；C 血压下降时开静脉给生理盐水；D 用苯二氮卓类让他安静并预防抽搐。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is D. The textbook makes benzodiazepines the first-line drug for stimulant agitation, high blood pressure, fast heart rate and seizures, but benzodiazepines aren't on the BC licensing exam for EMRs or PCPs. Oxygen, A, and active cooling, B, are open to every licence level, and cooling matters because high body temperature can kill these patients. An IV with normal saline, C, is a BC PCP intervention for low blood pressure. So your BC plan is safety, oxygen, cooling, monitoring, fluids if needed, and rapid transport.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 D。教材把苯二氮卓类作为兴奋剂引起的激越、高血压、心动过速和抽搐的一线用药，但 EMR 和 PCP 执照考试都不考苯二氮卓类。A 给氧和 B 主动降温所有级别都能做，而且降温很重要，因为高体温可以致命。C 低血压时开静脉给生理盐水是 BC 的 PCP 处置。所以你的 BC 方案是：安全、给氧、降温、监测、需要时补液，并快速转运。

slides.title: Cannabis and hallucinogens
slides.body:
DrugWhat you seeYour care
Cannabis (THC)euphoria, red eyes, mild tachycardia; smoked 2–4 h, edibles longerreassurance
Spice (synthetic)psychosis, vomiting, tachycardia, seizuressupport; fluids, antiemetic
LSD, mushroomsdistorted senses; "bad trip" paniccalm, low stimulation
PCP, ketaminedissociation; PCP: violence, no painsafety first; watch breathing
slides.say: Cannabis rarely causes serious medical problems. Smoked, it lasts two to four hours; eaten, it starts hours later and lasts about twice as long. New users may panic, and reassurance usually works. Synthetic cannabinoids, sold as spice, are far more dangerous: psychosis, a fast pulse, vomiting, kidney problems and seizures. The book suggests fluids and antiemetics, and as a PCP that's your Nausea–Vomiting protocol. LSD and mushrooms distort the senses; for a bad trip, keep things calm and quiet, with no lights or sirens. PCP and ketamine are dissociative drugs. PCP can make a patient violent and numb to pain, so protect yourself first. Ketamine can switch suddenly to deep sedation with slow breathing.
slides.sayZh: 大麻很少引起严重的医疗问题。吸食持续两到四小时；吃下去要几个小时才起效，持续时间约加倍。新手可能惊恐，安抚通常就够了。合成大麻素（spice）危险得多：精神病性症状、心率快、呕吐、肾损害和抽搐；书里建议补液和止吐，作为 PCP 这就是你的恶心呕吐流程。LSD 和蘑菇会扭曲感官；遇到「坏旅程」，要保持安静平和，不开警灯警笛。PCP（苯环利定）和氯胺酮是解离性药物：PCP 会让病人暴力、对疼痛没感觉，先保护好自己；氯胺酮可能突然转为深度镇静、呼吸变慢。

slides.title: Sedatives: benzos, barbiturates, GHB
slides.body:
• All boost GABA, the brain's main brake
  • Benzo alone: drowsy, slurred, unsteady; rarely deadly
  • Severe breathing problems or coma? Think alcohol or opioids too
  • GHB: odourless in a drink; acts in 30–60 min; LOC goes up and down
  • Care: airway, O₂, assist ventilation, transport
  • Book's antidote flumazenil: not routine (seizures); not on the BC exam list
slides.say: Sedative-hypnotics calm people down or put them to sleep. Benzodiazepines, barbiturates, sleeping pills and GHB all boost GABA, the brain's main brake. A benzodiazepine overdose on its own usually causes drowsiness, slurred speech and poor balance, and it's rarely deadly. So if your patient has severe breathing depression, low blood pressure or coma, think of a second drug, like alcohol or an opioid. GHB has no colour or smell and can be slipped into a drink. It acts in thirty to sixty minutes, causes memory loss, and the level of consciousness can go up and down, so watch the airway closely. The book's antidote, flumazenil, isn't routine because it can trigger seizures, and it isn't on the BC exam drug list.
slides.sayZh: 镇静催眠药让人平静或入睡。苯二氮卓类、巴比妥类、安眠药和 GHB 都增强 GABA，也就是大脑的主要「刹车」。单纯苯二氮卓过量通常是嗜睡、口齿不清、站不稳，很少致命。所以如果病人有严重的呼吸抑制、低血压或昏迷，要想到还有第二种药，比如酒精或阿片类。GHB 无色无味，可以被偷偷放进饮料，三十到六十分钟起效，会导致失忆，意识水平时好时坏，所以要紧盯气道。书里的解毒剂氟马西尼可能诱发抽搐，不常规使用，也不在 BC 考试药物清单上。

slides.title: Opioids: the toxidrome and the crisis
slides.body:
Pinpoint pupils + slow, shallow breathing + decreased LOC

  • BC also lists low BP, hypothermia, tachycardia
  • Jan 2016 – Dec 2018: over 11,500 opioid deaths in Canada
  • Nearly 3 in 4 from fentanyl and its analogues
  • Carfentanil hides in other drugs
  • Death usually comes from respiratory arrest
slides.say: The opioid toxidrome is the one you'll see most: pinpoint pupils, slow and shallow breathing, and a decreased level of consciousness. The BC protocol also lists low blood pressure, low body temperature and a fast heart rate as possible signs. Canada declared an opioid crisis in two thousand sixteen. From January two thousand sixteen to December two thousand eighteen, more than eleven thousand five hundred people died, and nearly three in four of those deaths involved fentanyl or similar drugs. Carfentanil, an animal tranquilizer far stronger than fentanyl, is now found mixed into other drugs without the user knowing. Opioids kill mainly by stopping breathing; the heart stops later, from lack of oxygen.
slides.sayZh: 阿片类中毒综合征是你最常见到的：针尖样瞳孔、呼吸慢而浅、意识水平下降。BC 流程还列出低血压、低体温和心动过速作为可能的表现。加拿大在二零一六年宣布阿片危机。二零一六年一月到二零一八年十二月，有超过一万一千五百人死亡，其中近四分之三与芬太尼及其类似物有关。卡芬太尼是一种比芬太尼强得多的动物镇静剂，现在被混进其他毒品里，使用者自己并不知道。阿片类主要通过让人停止呼吸致死，心脏是之后因缺氧才停的。

slides.title: Ventilation comes first
slides.body:
Slow breathing→low O₂, high CO₂→deeper coma
  • Breathing can drop to 4–5 a minute
  • Position, suction, OPA, BVM with O₂
  • Two-person BVM when you can
  • Lowering CO₂ alone can wake the patient up
  • Check the BGL; correct a low glucose
slides.say: Before any drug, fix the breathing. An opioid patient may breathe only four or five times a minute. Oxygen falls, carbon dioxide builds up, and high carbon dioxide deepens the coma; this is called carbon dioxide narcosis. A floppy tongue makes it worse. So open the airway, suction, insert an oral airway, and ventilate with a bag-valve mask and oxygen; BC suggests a two-person technique when possible. Often, just lowering the carbon dioxide improves the level of consciousness, before any naloxone. This is your EMR skill, and it stays the most important step at PCP level. Then take vital signs, including a glucose, and correct a low glucose, because low sugar can look exactly like an overdose.
slides.sayZh: 用药之前，先解决呼吸。阿片类病人每分钟可能只呼吸四五次：氧下降、二氧化碳堆积，而高二氧化碳会让昏迷更深，这叫二氧化碳麻醉；舌后坠会让情况更糟。所以要开放气道、吸引、放口咽通气道，用球囊面罩加氧气通气；BC 建议尽可能用双人法。很多时候，光是把二氧化碳降下来，意识就会好转，还没用纳洛酮。这是你的 EMR 技能，在 PCP 级别仍是最重要的一步。然后测生命体征，包括血糖，并纠正低血糖，因为低血糖可以和过量一模一样。

slides.title: EMR vs PCP: Suspected Narcotic Overdose
slides.body:
Decreased LOC + depressed breathing (slow rate and small tidal volume)

All licence levels (EMR + PCP)

  • Airway: position, suction, adjuncts
  • Support ventilation; consider two-person BVM
  • O₂ to SpO₂ ≥ 94%
  • History, vitals, BGL; correct a low glucose
  • Give naloxone
  • Transport; reassess en route

PCP adds

  • Still unconscious and apneic?
  • Consider vascular access
  • Give naloxone IV
slides.say: Here's the BC Suspected Narcotic Overdose protocol. Notice how much of it every licence level already does. Manage the airway with positioning, suction and adjuncts. Support ventilation, using a two-person bag-valve-mask technique when you can. Give oxygen to a saturation of ninety-four percent or higher. Take a history and vital signs, including blood glucose, and correct a low glucose. Give naloxone, then transport and keep reassessing. The PCP column is short but important. If the patient remains unconscious and apneic, which means not breathing, consider an IV and give naloxone intravenously. IV naloxone works in about one minute, compared with about three minutes for the IM and intranasal routes.
slides.sayZh: 这是 BC 的疑似阿片类过量流程。注意，其中很多是所有级别都已经在做的：用体位、吸引和辅助装置管理气道；支持通气，尽可能用双人球囊面罩；给氧使血氧达到九十四以上；问病史、测生命体征，包括血糖，纠正低血糖；给纳洛酮，然后转运并持续复评。PCP 一栏很短但很关键：如果病人仍然昏迷、呼吸暂停，也就是没有呼吸，考虑开静脉，静脉给纳洛酮。静脉纳洛酮约一分钟起效，肌注和鼻内约三分钟。

slides.title: The BC naloxone ladder
slides.body:
StepDoseRoute
10.4 mgIM or IV
2 (after 3 min)0.4 mgIM or IV
3 (after 3 min)0.8 mgIM or IV
4 (after 3 min)2.0 mgIM or IV
Or4 mgIN

Next dose only if SpO₂ ≥ 94% and breathing over 10 a minute are not yet reached. Goal: breathing, not a wide-awake patient.
slides.say: Here is the BC naloxone ladder. Start with point four milligrams, IM or IV. Wait three minutes. If the saturation still isn't ninety-four percent or higher, with breathing over ten a minute, give another point four. Then point eight, then two milligrams, each after another three minutes. The intranasal option is four milligrams. Notice the goal: good oxygen and breathing, not a wide-awake patient. Naloxone pushes the opioid off its receptors, and too much at once can throw a long-term user into sudden withdrawal: vomiting, sweating, a racing heart and combativeness. The book says opioid withdrawal itself isn't life-threatening, but an angry patient who refuses care is a real danger.
slides.sayZh: 这是 BC 的纳洛酮阶梯。先给零点四毫克，IM 或 IV。等三分钟，如果血氧仍未达到九十四以上、呼吸未超过每分钟十次，再给零点四；然后是零点八，再然后是两毫克，每次间隔三分钟。鼻内给药是四毫克。注意目标：氧合和呼吸足够，而不是让病人完全清醒。纳洛酮把阿片类从受体上挤下来，一次给太多会让长期使用者突然戒断：呕吐、出汗、心跳飞快和攻击性。书里说阿片戒断本身不危及生命，但一个愤怒、拒绝救治的病人是真正的危险。

slides.q: You're a PCP. An unresponsive man has pinpoint pupils and is not breathing. You are ventilating with a BVM and have given naloxone 0.4 mg IM twice, 3 minutes apart. He is still unconscious and apneic. What is your best next step?
options: Give 2.0 mg IM now, skipping the 0.8 mg step
Keep ventilating, start an IV, and give naloxone 0.8 mg IV
Stop ventilating for a minute to see if he breathes on his own
Give a benzodiazepine in case it's a sedative overdose
slides.say: Now a PCP decision. You're a PCP. An unresponsive man has pinpoint pupils and is not breathing. You're ventilating with a bag-valve mask and have given naloxone point four milligrams IM twice, three minutes apart. He's still unconscious and apneic. What's your best next step? A, give two milligrams IM now, skipping the point eight step. B, keep ventilating, start an IV, and give naloxone point eight milligrams IV. C, stop ventilating for a minute to see if he breathes on his own. D, give a benzodiazepine in case it's a sedative overdose. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 来一道 PCP 决策题。你是 PCP。一名无反应的男子瞳孔针尖样、没有呼吸。你正在用球囊面罩通气，已经肌注纳洛酮零点四毫克两次，间隔三分钟。他仍然昏迷、呼吸暂停。最好的下一步是什么？A 现在肌注两毫克，跳过零点八这一步；B 继续通气，开静脉，静脉给纳洛酮零点八毫克；C 停止通气一分钟，看他能不能自己呼吸；D 给苯二氮卓类，以防是镇静药过量。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is B. The next step on the BC ladder is point eight milligrams, and the PCP part of the protocol says that with continued unconsciousness and apnea you consider an IV and give naloxone intravenously, which acts in about one minute. Ventilation never stops while you do it. A skips a step on the ladder. C is dangerous: he isn't breathing, so stopping ventilation makes him more hypoxic. D is wrong because benzodiazepines aren't on the BC licensing exam, and they would depress his breathing even more.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 B。BC 阶梯的下一步是零点八毫克，而流程中 PCP 的部分说明：持续昏迷且呼吸暂停时，考虑开静脉、静脉给纳洛酮，约一分钟起效。整个过程中通气不能停。A 跳过了阶梯中的一步；C 很危险，他没有呼吸，停止通气只会让缺氧更重；D 错在苯二氮卓类执照考试不考，而且会进一步抑制呼吸。

slides.title: New for you as a PCP: watch out for
slides.body:
• Naloxone wears off before many opioids: expect re-sedation
  • Book: don't let a patient refuse transport after naloxone
  • IV in a waking patient: withdrawal, combativeness, needle safety
  • No response? Think stroke, head injury, low sugar, mixed drugs
  • Overdose arrest = asphyxia: alone with an AED, 5 cycles CPR first
slides.say: Here are the watch-outs that come with your new responsibilities. Naloxone wears off sooner than many opioids, so a patient who wakes up can slip back into a coma, and repeat doses are common. That's why the book says a patient shouldn't be allowed to refuse transport after naloxone. When you start an IV on a patient who is waking up, expect withdrawal and possible combativeness, and protect yourself and your needle. If there's no response to naloxone, think wider: a stroke, a head injury, low sugar, or a mix of drugs. And if the patient arrests, it's an asphyxia arrest: in BC, if you're alone with an AED, give five cycles of CPR, about two minutes, before applying it.
slides.sayZh: 随着新的职责而来的注意事项：纳洛酮的作用比很多阿片类消失得早，醒过来的病人可能再次昏迷，重复给药很常见。所以书里说，用过纳洛酮的病人不应被允许拒绝转运。给正在醒来的病人开静脉时，要预料到戒断和可能的攻击，保护好自己和针头。如果对纳洛酮没反应，要想得更广：卒中、颅脑损伤、低血糖或多药混用。如果病人心脏骤停，这是窒息性骤停：在 BC，如果你一个人带着 AED，先做五个周期、约两分钟的 CPR，再接 AED。

slides.title: For the BC exam
slides.body:
• Book: naloxone IV 0.4–2 mg titrated → BC: 0.4 → 0.4 → 0.8 → 2.0 mg IM/IV, or 4 mg IN
  • Ventilate first, then naloxone
  • Benzodiazepines: not on the BC exam
  • Thiamine, flumazenil, opioid painkillers: not on the exam (BCEHS added scope: opioids)
  • BC protocol airway: position, suction, adjuncts, BVM
slides.say: Now the BC exam points. The book gives naloxone IV, point four to two milligrams, titrated. BC uses a fixed ladder: point four, point four, point eight, two milligrams, IM or IV, three minutes apart, or four milligrams intranasal, and you ventilate first. The book reaches for benzodiazepines again and again, for stimulants, seizures and alcohol withdrawal, but they aren't on the BC licensing exam. Thiamine, flumazenil and opioid painkillers aren't on it either, though BCEHS PCPs may give opioids after added-scope training. And where the book suggests an advanced airway for the overdose patient, the BC protocol lists positioning, suction, adjuncts and bag-valve-mask ventilation. Know the BC version for your exams.
slides.sayZh: 现在看 BC 考点。书里是静脉纳洛酮零点四到两毫克滴定。BC 用固定阶梯：零点四、零点四、零点八、两毫克，IM 或 IV，每次间隔三分钟，或鼻内四毫克，而且先通气。书里在兴奋剂、抽搐和酒精戒断中反复使用苯二氮卓类，但执照考试不考它们。硫胺素、氟马西尼和阿片类止痛药也都不考；其中阿片类，BCEHS 的 PCP 经扩展范围（Schedule 1/2）培训后可以用。书里对过量病人建议高级气道，而 BC 流程列出的是体位、吸引、辅助装置和球囊面罩通气。考试要按 BC 的版本答。

slides.title: Three things to remember
slides.body:
1. Alcohol, sedatives, opioids kill by breathing: airway, BVM, BGL
  2. Stimulants: safety, cooling, O₂, fluids; no benzodiazepines on the BC exam
  3. Naloxone 0.4 → 0.4 → 0.8 → 2.0 mg or 4 mg IN; PCP adds IV if still apneic

Next: gases, pesticides, household poisons, prescription drugs and bites
slides.say: Three things to remember. One: alcohol, sedatives and opioids all kill mainly by depressing breathing, so your airway, your bag-valve mask and a glucose check come first. Two: stimulant patients need safety, cooling, oxygen, and fluids if hypotensive; the book's benzodiazepines aren't on the BC exam. Three: the BC naloxone ladder is point four, point four, point eight, then two milligrams, IM or IV, three minutes apart, or four milligrams intranasal, aiming for good oxygen and breathing over ten. As a PCP, you add IV naloxone if the patient stays unconscious and apneic. Next lesson: toxic gases, pesticides, household poisons, prescription drugs, and bites and stings. If anything was unclear, tap Ask.
slides.sayZh: 记住三件事。一，酒精、镇静药和阿片类主要通过抑制呼吸致死，所以气道、球囊面罩和测血糖放在最前面。二，兴奋剂病人需要安全、降温、给氧，低血压时补液；书里的苯二氮卓类执照考试不考。三，BC 纳洛酮阶梯是零点四、零点四、零点八、两毫克，IM 或 IV，每次间隔三分钟，或鼻内四毫克，目标是氧合良好、呼吸超过每分钟十次；作为 PCP，病人持续昏迷、呼吸暂停时你可以静脉给纳洛酮。下节课：有毒气体、农药、家用毒物、处方药，以及咬伤蜇伤。有不懂的点「Ask」。
